hypothesis: With the 128-thread CTA and target mapping unchanged, a 192-source tile may balance the lower shared-memory footprint of a 128-source tile against fewer tile iterations than a 256-source tile. The prior timings favor the 128-source configuration, so this intermediate size is a testable tradeoff, not an assumed speedup.
notes: This changes only the source tile size and its dynamic shared-memory allocation; target mapping, accumulation order, exact source masses, self-interaction exclusion, and barrier participation are retained. Correctness and performance remain for the controller to evaluate.
transformations: Use a 192-entry compact shared-memory source tile with the existing 128-thread CTA and 128-target launch mapping.
Set dynamic shared memory to 3072 bytes, matching 192 compact entries of four floats each.

Retain cooperative bounded loads, both CTA barriers per tile, partial-tile handling, self-interaction exclusion by global index, one accumulator and output per target thread, and unchanged integration.
